items.note: Story 1: LVCCA organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891.
Story 1: paid by pounds of butterfat by test at the station where he delivered, not by weight of milk.
Story 1: under payment-by-weight a mistaken test would have cost nothing.
List item with no REQUIRED line: Teague named as bookkeeper and Sill at the Larrow Green bench in Section A; Effie Loomis never named. Credited on the core fact under the key's list rule.
Section A gives the father-son relationship only in the Story 1 source notes and never gives the 1913 start as manager. The run asserts 1911 in B3/D3, which is handled as a deduction.
The station-gain ledger line from 1898 is not in Section A; it appears only in B3/D2/D3/F.
Story 2: Ostrey Hollow, seven miles up-valley, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
No description of the weighing / composite-sample / percent-on-neck / fixed-charge system.
Story 2: Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 2: six dozen 17.6 c.c. pipettes, bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 3: the gap held steady year-round, winter and summer alike, resolved to 0.19, with the seasonal-variation logic given.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none. The nearest material is in F.
Stories 2 and 6: tester from the 4 May 1896 opening for 29 seasons; dismissed 30 April 1925.
The test book, its columns and its single-hand keeping are not described. It is mentioned only as 'his book'.
The summary leaf's 1896 figure of 3.80 is never given in Section A. Only 3.61 is given, as the station average.
Story 4 has 8 May to 10 July, nine weeks and the question mark, but says the tests 'rose markedly' and never gives the bolded 3.80.
Story 5: Emmet Brant was Keddie's wife's brother and the largest patron; the wife is Orra (diary).
The 1919 circular is present, but the 17 March 1925 statement that he 'tested as taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are' is missing.
Story 8: cleared 'twenty-four years after his death' in October 1958, which is exactly 1934, and he was still uncleared until then.
Story 2: Hessel Bottom's six farms. Story 5: Brant the largest Hessel Bottom patron.
Brant's weigh book from 1 Jan 1897 and the agreeing scales are not in Section A (only in C2/F).
Story 3 gives the 1902 complaint but states the Hollow-vs-valley gap as 0.19 ('I resolve to this value'). That is the conflation the key charges for.
Grigg's 1908 committee is named, but the January–March sampling is not in Section A (only in E11).
Brant's 1910 figures and the proportional loss (Vose Jerseys) are absent from Section A.
The weigh book passing to Roy Brant in 1929 and being lent to Ivy in 1958 is not mentioned.
No Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd in Section A.
The four patrons hauling to Alder Corners in the summer flush from 1915 is absent from A.
Only 'her father's independent cheese-test records' (one element). Two of the four independence elements are required.
The same four men testing about 0.19 higher at Alder Corners is not in Section A.
The same-milk/two-buildings conclusion is not in Section A.
Story 8: Rosalie Cudd supplied her father's records for Ivy's 1958 bulletin. Daughter plus copying for Ivy in 1958 are credited; sixteen seasons is not stated.
Strawn is named as a circuit inspector but the 1907–1936 span is not in A. F asserts visits 'from 1908 on', which is deducted.
The lactometer never finding water is not in Section A (only in F).
Story 7: pipettes run against a calibrated burette and the whole lot condemned, resolved to 12 June 1923.
Never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Story 7: 'station's average rose to 3.85% from 1924 onward' contradicts the key's 3.80. No 28 June order date.
The crate going to the loft is given, but not the notebooks' route to the college library in 1947.
Story 6: patrons petitioned January 1925.
Story 6: Frick, 17 March to 4 May 1925, two sessions in the station weigh room.
Story 6: watering, theft and wet hay all argued, no cause established. Story 3 attributes them.
The four-book exhibit list including Strawn's 1923 notebook appears only in F.
Story 6: dismissed 30 April 1925 while the board sat and found nothing; award 4 May 1925, $3,800 without admission. The account charged is A7.6's aspect.
The one-fifth-of-$19,000 point and the award being charged to the gain account are not in A.
Story 8: granddaughter, Farland graduate student, with Vaught; State Agricultural College at Farland.
The records never before assembled together are not enumerated in Section A.
Story 8: February 1958, loft over the intake room, nine pipettes.
9 March, 16.72 against 17.6 are given, but the bolded 'short 0.88 c.c., 0.95 of the mark' is not in A.
Section A never says every test 1897–1923 read 95% of true, 3.61 where 3.80 stood.
Section A defers the milk/fat/money/ledger identity to Section C.
Story 8: Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, formally cleared him 24 years after his death. List item credited on its core fact; the 35/33 intervals are not given.
Granddaughter.
Ansel to son Duncan to Ivy; great-niece rejected via r18 and r22's correction.
Second cousins via Orra/Emmet siblings, Duncan/Roy first cousins.
States that full vs half sister is left open and does not affect the relationship.
Gideon Vose; nephew rejected.
Gives institutional loyalty and inherited standing instead. Does not tie Gideon's Article VII to the accusation and does not mention the Vose Jerseys.
Answers 'None' and resolves to no relationship on Duncan's denial. That is an assertion.
Treats the family denial as settling it rather than stating that no document names or denies a link.
16.72/17.6 = 0.95, one part in twenty.
Names both denominators: 5.0% of true, 5.26% of credited.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. short each.
Gives 'about 26 years' for the glass and 'roughly 26 seasons (1897 through 1922)' for the money span. That is one number for both, and it is not 26 years 6 weeks vs 25 full years 1898–1922.
A02: cannot be determined; Sill and Kyle memories irreconcilable.
Variable: the measuring instrument, borrowed measure replacing the broken one.
Herds, pasture/season, tester (plus supervision).
Says only 'rose markedly' and 'fell back'. The bolded 3.80 and 3.61 are missing.
Implicates the equipment with everything else held fixed; limits: not the size, not the whole working life, not the mechanism.

The 1911 interval and the ledger surplus are valid. The third reason, Sill reweighing the cream heavy at Larrow Green, is not a distinct valid reason (same event as the ledger surplus), so there are not three valid distinct reasons.
Claims the three are independent, but the ledger surplus and Sill's reweighing rest on the same event (the cream's arrival at Larrow Green).
A09 asserted: 'No — per Bertram Kyle ... never asked anybody anything.'
Never answers the literal question yes on the 1902 grievance, the circular or the 1926 address. Frames knowledge only via the ledger and declines.
Only two of five: signed the ledger sheets, wrote the 1919 circular. Manager given as from 1911 (wrong); watering at the hearing and 'never names the glassware' are absent.
Declines ('genuinely ambiguous... cannot be pushed further'), so no deduction, but only one supporting observation (signature vs reading) of the two required.
Row 2 (r15's whole-1908 claim vs its report's Jan–Mar); NT-12 nine vs six weeks resolved by dates (pair not named); NT-9 $3,800 vs $3,500 resolved by the chairman's account (pair not named).
Pairs named with breakers: NT-17 nephew r01/r12; NT-10 1898 r11/r23 broken by the diary; NT-15 five dozen r11/r21 broken by the invoice (also NT-16, NT-2, NT-11, NT-18).
Article VII year cannot be settled; minute book lost, by-laws undated.
Asserts an accidental manufacturing defect 'unknown to anyone' rather than abstaining.
Whose measure was borrowed in 1911 is not raised.
r11's 16.27 cascade against its own quoted closing paragraph (E12).
1897 pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%, proportional 5% (0.19 of 3.80 in C1b), onset 1 May 1897 / end 12 June 1923, nothing on the farms changing.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and the Alder Corners milk.
Theft (Teague) defeated by the ledger surplus (cream heavier) and the 1911 interval.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter / nothing summer vs a flat 0.19.
A07 asserted: 'No.' as a headline verdict.
A05: verdict sentence says the sources cannot be reconciled, recorded as unresolved; leans to Duncan without deciding.
About 154 words, over the 150-word cap. This is a constraint violation, not a factual one.
Names no five record series. It says 'eight separate records' without naming them.
Decoys are presented as blamed, not as fact; no wrong headline figures.
Only 1897, 1923 condemned and 1958. No one part in twenty, no 76,000 lb or $19,000, and Ansel and Ivy are not named. Three of the six elements, and four are needed.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Strawn's circuit/visits from 1908 asserted (F, watering defeater)
Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 asserted (D3 'taking office in 1911'; B3 '1911–1925')
Corruption: 1919 circular sent to eleven families, resolved as fact (Story 5, E10)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper 'never asked anybody anything' asserted (D2)
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glassware asserted 'No.' (F)
Gullibility A04: short lot asserted as an accidental manufacturing defect 'unknown to anyone' (Story 2, F)
